meta.title: GLP-1 Dosage Chart: Semaglutide & Tirzepatide Steps by Label
meta.description: Semaglutide and tirzepatide dosage chart from each US label: start, weeks per step, maintenance, maximum and mL for Wegovy, Ozempic, Mounjaro and Zepbound.

strings: GLP-1 dosage chart: the titration steps each US label lists
By Ümit Can Erim · Published 9 October 2026 · Updated 4 November 2026 · Sources checked 4 November 2026 · How these guides are written

Search for a semaglutide or tirzepatide dosage chart and you will find plenty of them, most without a source. Below are the steps exactly as each product's US prescribing information lists them, with the section they come from. Read them for what they are: the starting point and the slowest increases a label sets out, written to reduce stomach side effects. They are not a plan. Your prescriber decides when you move up, whether you stay, and whether you go back, and the leaflet in your own country may say something different.

Read this first. These tables reproduce the US labels on DailyMed as of 4 November 2026. The same brand can have different indications, strengths and steps in the UK, the EU or Turkey. Do not use this page to change a dose or to move to the next step on your own; if a step is hard to tolerate, that is a conversation with your prescriber.
GLP-1 dosage chart at a glance

Titration means starting low and raising the dose in steps; the US labels below do it to reduce the risk of stomach and gut side effects. Weekly injections move up after 4 weeks at the earliest, and daily tablets after 30 days. The chart lists each product's start, time on each step, maintenance and highest strength. The full steps follow.
7.2 mg for adult weight reduction; otherwise 2.4 mg
15 mg in adults; 10 mg in children aged 10 and over
5, 10 or 15 mg for weight reduction; 10 or 15 mg for obstructive sleep apnoea
Source: section 2 of each US prescribing information, checked on 4 November 2026 [1–6]. Time on each step is the shortest the label lists, not a target.

Three things in the labels' own wording change how a chart should be read. First, intervals are minimums: "after at least 4 weeks" means no sooner, not "on week 5". Second, several labels say that if a step is not tolerated, the prescriber may consider delaying the next one or choosing a lower maintenance dose. Third, maintenance is often a range rather than a finish line, chosen on response and tolerability. A chart that shows one arrow to the top strength leaves all three out.
Maintenance: 1.7 mg or 2.4 mg, depending on the indication

Source: Wegovy US prescribing information, section 2.2, Table 1 [1]. For weight reduction in adults, the label adds that after at least 4 weeks at 2.4 mg, where further reduction is clinically indicated, the dose may go up to a maximum of 7.2 mg.
After at least 4 weeks on 0.5 mg, if more glucose control is needed
After at least 4 weeks on 1 mg, if more is needed
Source: Ozempic US prescribing information, section 2.2 [2]. For type 2 diabetes with chronic kidney disease, the label lists 1 mg as the maintenance dose, after at least 4 weeks on 0.5 mg.
Each increase, if more glucose control is needed
+2.5 mg, after at least 4 weeks on the current dose
Source: Mounjaro US prescribing information, section 2.1 [3]. In the EU, Mounjaro is also authorised for weight management, under its own product information [7].
2.5 mg (initiation only, not approved as a maintenance dose)
Source: Zepbound US prescribing information, sections 2.1–2.2 [4].
Source: Wegovy US prescribing information, section 2.3, Table 2 [1]. How the tablet is taken (empty stomach, water only, 30-minute wait) is covered in the Wegovy pill guide.
Ozempic® tablets and Rybelsus® (oral semaglutide, daily, type 2 diabetes)
4 mg, or 9 mg if more glucose control is needed
7 mg, or 14 mg if more glucose control is needed

Source: Ozempic tablets and Rybelsus US prescribing information, section 2.2 [5]. The label says the starting strength of each is not effective for glucose control and is there for initiation, and that the two products are not interchangeable milligram for milligram.
After at least 30 days on 0.8 mg
After at least 30 days on 2.5 mg
Further steps, based on response and tolerability
9 mg, 14.5 mg, 17.2 mg, each after at least 30 days on the current dose

Source: Foundayo US prescribing information, sections 2.1–2.2 [6]. The label caps the dose lower (9 mg) when it is taken with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, a group of other medicines, which is one more reason the right step depends on your whole medicine list.
GLP-1 dosing chart in mL: what each device holds

Milligrams are the dose. Millilitres only say how much liquid carries it, and that changes with the product and the device: 2.5 mg of tirzepatide is 0.5 mL in a single-dose pen and 0.6 mL in a multi-dose vial. These are the volumes each label lists.
Mounjaro® or Zepbound® single-dose pen or vial

Source: section 3 of each US prescribing information [1–4]. Do not use this table to measure a dose. Compounded products are not on these labels and their strength per mL varies, so these volumes do not apply to them; go by your prescription and ask your pharmacist. See why units and milligrams have no single conversion.
GLP-1 dose conversion: the only switches the labels spell out

A chart that turns any GLP-1 dose into another does not exist on these labels. They give no equivalent dose between semaglutide and tirzepatide, and the dosing sections of the Mounjaro, Zepbound and Foundayo labels list no switching schedule. The semaglutide labels describe only the switches below, between their own products.
One week after stopping the injection
The day after stopping the tablets
Ozempic® tablets 4 mg, or the reverse
The day after stopping; not during the first 30 days
Ozempic® tablets 9 mg, or the reverse

Source: Wegovy US prescribing information, section 2.5 [1]; Ozempic tablets and Rybelsus US prescribing information, sections 2.3–2.4 [5]. Whether to switch, and to what, is your prescriber's decision.

The indication changes the schedule. Ozempic and Wegovy are the same molecule with different steps and different maximums, because one label is written for blood glucose and the other for weight. Gaps change it too: the Wegovy injection label tells prescribers to restart escalation at a lower dose after two or more consecutive missed doses, and the Foundayo label says the same after seven or more consecutive missed tablets. What to do after a single missed dose is different again for each product; it is quoted in what each leaflet says about a missed dose. None of that fits in a chart, and all of it is your prescriber's to apply.
Recording the step you are actually on

The useful record is not the label's schedule; it is yours. Which strength, from which date, how long you stayed, and what happened when you moved up. Dozify records the dose your prescriber set and the date of every dose; it never proposes one and does not plan the next step. For injections, the Premium medication-level view is an estimate modelled from your logged doses, never a measurement, and it is not drawn for tablets (how the estimate works). When the appointment comes, the history is what answers "when did you go up to this dose?", and the Premium doctor report puts it on paper.

Every dose, every step and the day it started, in one place on your phone. Dozify records what you and your prescriber decided; it never proposes a dose.
How often are GLP-1 doses increased?

On these US labels, weekly injections step up after 4 weeks at the earliest and daily tablets after 30 days. Later steps are often conditional: the Ozempic®, Mounjaro® and Foundayo™ labels tie them to glucose control or to response and tolerability. Your prescriber can also keep you on a step for longer.
What is a GLP-1 maintenance dose?

It is the strength you stay on after the step-up. Labels often list more than one: 1.7 or 2.4 mg for Wegovy® injection, 0.5, 1 or 2 mg for Ozempic® injection, and 5, 10 or 15 mg for Zepbound® in weight reduction. Your prescriber chooses, using the label's criteria such as response, tolerability or glucose control.
How many dose steps do semaglutide and tirzepatide have?

Counting increases from the starting dose: Wegovy® injection reaches 2.4 mg after 4 increases, at week 17. Ozempic® injection reaches 2 mg after 3, at week 13 at the earliest. Mounjaro® and Zepbound® reach 15 mg after 5, at week 21 at the earliest. Those are the shortest routes the labels allow, not where everyone ends up.
Is there a chart to convert semaglutide to tirzepatide?
Not on these labels. None of them lists an equivalent dose between the two medicines. If you are changing medicine, the new starting dose is your prescriber's decision.
Can I move to the next step sooner if I feel fine?
The labels give minimum intervals ("at least 4 weeks", "at least 30 days"), not targets to beat. Any change to timing is your prescriber's decision.
Is the semaglutide chart the same for Ozempic® and Wegovy®?
No. The first steps look alike, but the labels diverge after that: different later steps, different maintenance doses and different maximums, because they are prescribed for different conditions.
Why does Zepbound® start at a dose that is not approved for maintenance?

The label describes 2.5 mg as being for starting treatment only, and frames the escalation as a way to reduce the risk of stomach and gut side effects. It does not describe the starting dose as the one meant to do the work.
Do these steps apply in the UK, the EU or Turkey?
Not necessarily. Each regulator approves its own label, and indications, strengths and steps can differ. The leaflet in your box and your prescriber are the authority where you live.
A step is making me feel unwell. Should I go back down?

Several labels give prescribers that option, or the option of waiting longer before the next step, which is exactly why it should be their call. Tell them what happened and when; a dated log makes that conversation shorter. If symptoms are severe, seek medical care.

Educational information, not medical advice. Dozify is a personal tracking app, not a medical device. This page reproduces the escalation steps in public US prescribing information and does not recommend a dose, a schedule or a course of action for any individual. Always follow the instructions that came with your medication and your prescriber's directions. If you have severe symptoms, seek medical care or call your local emergency number.
